knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r}
library(RcmdrShiny)
```

# Overview

The Workbench is the part of Studio that works **outside the dialogs**: Script,
Console, Output, Messages, Environment and Models. They all use the same
engine: `run_command()`, `state$history`, `state$output`, `state$messages` and
`state$env`.

Script, Console and dialogs are therefore three ways to run the same R
commands, with the same log and the same objects.

# Script cells

The Script tab splits a plain R script into cells that follow the top-level
expressions. A multi-line call stays in one cell.

```{r}
text <- paste(
  "# Data preparation",
  "D$z <- D$x * 2",
  "",
  "fit <- lm(y ~ x, data = D)",
  "",
  "summary(fit)",
  sep = "\n"
)
cells <- RcmdrShiny:::script_cells(text, "r")
cells[, c("id", "label", "start", "end")]
```

Cells can be selected by a zero-based editor row, and "run above" and "run
below" take whole cells only.

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::script_cell_at(cells, 4)$id
RcmdrShiny:::script_cells_above(cells, 4)$id
RcmdrShiny:::script_cells_below(cells, 4)$id
```

In R Markdown and knitr documents the cells are the code chunks.

```{r}
rmd <- c("## Section", "", "```{r one}", "1 + 1", "```")
RcmdrShiny:::script_cells(paste(rmd, collapse = "\n"), "rmd")
```

Running a cell goes through the command engine with `log = FALSE`, so it is
recorded in the structured history without duplicating the code into the
script.

```{r}
state <- AppState()
state$env$D <- data.frame(y = c(2, 1, 4, 3), x = c(2, 4, 6, 8))
RcmdrShiny:::script_run_cell(state, cells[2, , drop = FALSE])$status
```

# Outline and diagnostics

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::script_outline(text, "r")
RcmdrShiny:::script_diagnostics("x <- (1 + ")
```

# Formatting

Formatting is optional and explicit. `styler` is a Suggests dependency.

```{r}
result <- RcmdrShiny:::script_format_text("x<-1")
result$changed
```

# Console

The console keeps its own recall history and records every command in the
structured history.

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::console_execute(state, "mean(D$y)")$status
RcmdrShiny:::console_history_recall(state, -1)
RcmdrShiny:::console_execute(state, "readline('name? ')")$status
```

The last call is `blocked`: interactive prompts cannot be answered from a
browser, so the console refuses to start them.

# Output and Messages

History entries carry enough metadata to build output cards and filter them.

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::history_filter_entries(state$history, "", "console", "ok")
RcmdrShiny:::messages_as_data_frame(state)
```

A warning becomes a structured message.

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::run_command(state, "warning('careful')")
RcmdrShiny:::messages_filter(state$message_entries, "", "warning")
```

# Environment

The object explorer renders metadata only and previews objects without running
a command.

```{r}
objects <- RcmdrShiny:::object_list(state)
objects[, c("name", "class", "type")]
cat(RcmdrShiny:::object_preview(state, "D"))
```

Actions that print or change the session are reproducible.

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::object_action(state, "D", "summary")
tail(state$log, 1)
```

# Models

The registry recognises the model classes created by the dialogs and the
console.

```{r}
state$env$fit <- stats::lm(y ~ x, data = state$env$D)
models <- RcmdrShiny:::model_registry(state)
models[, c("name", "class", "formula", "n", "aic", "bic", "r2")]
```

Actions reuse the existing commands.

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::model_action(state, "fit", "summary")
tail(state$log, 1)
```

Reopening the dialog uses the memory stored with the fitting command, when it
exists.

# Design notes

- The three levels (dialogs, console, script) share one engine and one history.
- Cell output is session state; it is cleared when the script changes.
- The console guard prevents blocking commands instead of pretending to
  interrupt them.
- The object explorer never copies large objects.
- The model dashboard adds no statistical procedure: it orchestrates existing
  commands.
